Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The classes $[L(\lambda)]$, and separately the classes $[M(\lambda)]$, form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O)$. For a fixed finite central-character label set $\Lambda=W\cdot\lambda$, the transition between its standard and simple classes is unitriangular in any linear order extending $\leq$. This remains true on a downward-closed subset of that finite poset. It is not a claim about finite downward ideals of all of $\mathfrak h^*$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let
$\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection
$s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the
object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two
factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with
multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group
$$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$
Moreover $\theta_s$ is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects with finite
Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_sX$ has one with multiplicities
$(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$,
and the same formula holds in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$. The resulting flag is
not in general split; splitting is neither asserted nor used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block and
translation theory ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]).

Fix the dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ of a regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]) and an
integral weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and
$\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$ for a reflection
$s=s_\alpha$; this is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall translation
data, the published
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] being stated with
antidominant representatives, and the dominant standard counts below are
proved through the norm-distance and extremal-weight bounds
([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]],
[[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) rather than
by applying that datum literally. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant element of
the linear Weyl orbit of $\mu-\lambda$ and let
$E=L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\nu$, so
that $\mu-\lambda$ is an extremal weight of $E$; write
$E^{*}=L(-w_0\nu)$ for its dual
([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).

With $\chi_\lambda,\chi_\mu$ the generalized central characters and
$\operatorname{pr}$ the exact central projections of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], define the **onto-wall** and
**out-of-wall** translations
$$T_{\mathrm{on}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(E\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ(E^{*}\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}},$$
and the **wall-crossing functor**
$$\theta_s:=T_{\mathrm{out}}\circ T_{\mathrm{on}}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** Both translations are exact, and $T_{\mathrm{out}}$ is
both a left and a right adjoint of $T_{\mathrm{on}}$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]); hence
$\theta_s$ is exact and, as a composite of restriction-of-scalars and central
block projection applied to tensoring by $E^{*}\otimes E$, it is a natural
direct summand of the endofunctor
$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ((E^{*}\otimes E)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}$,
so it is a projective functor on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]. On
standard objects the dominant-chamber counts are
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and the
two-factor flag $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w\cdot s\cdot\lambda)]$ for
$T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, as follows directly from the tensor flag and the two norm bounds above.
Put $v=\lambda+\rho$, $u=\mu+\rho$. A retained onto-wall label satisfies
$wv+\gamma=xu$ with $|\gamma|\le|u-v|$. Thus
$|\gamma|=|v-w^{-1}xu|\ge|v-u|$; equality and regularity of $v$ give
$w^{-1}xu=u$, leaving the single label $w\cdot\mu$, with its extremal
weight of multiplicity one. For the return translation,
$wu+\delta=xv$ implies equality in $|u-w^{-1}xv|\ge|u-v|$, so
$w^{-1}xv\in\{v,sv\}$ and $x\in\{w,ws\}$, again with
extremal weights of multiplicity one. These calculations use the Verma
tensor flag of [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]].

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair
$(\theta_s,\eta,\varepsilon)$ is determined by the choice of the
biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct
$\theta_s$ or to generate objects.

For the geometric finite Weyl group and its simple reflections, define $u\le v$ when a reduced expression for $v$ contains a reduced expression for $u$ as an ordered subword: choose positions in increasing order, multiply their letters in that order, and require their number to be $\ell(u)$. The empty subword represents the identity.

The following proof shows this condition is independent of the reduced expression for $v$ and is equivalent to a chain $u=w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_k=v$ with $w_{j+1}=t_jw_j$, each $t_j$ a root reflection and $\ell(w_{j+1})=\ell(w_j)+1$. Thus it is a partial order, called **strong Bruhat order**. A zero-length chain is allowed. The subword and saturated-reflection-chain descriptions are proved equivalent here; neither an abstract Coxeter presentation nor weak order or inversion-set containment is being substituted.

derivations.claim: The map $c$ is a well-defined homomorphism: by [F1] the classes of the standards are a $\mathbb Z$-basis indexed by the $|W|$ elements of $W$; sending the basis element $[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]$ to $v$ therefore extends uniquely to an isomorphism of free abelian groups of rank $|W|$.

On every Verma class the formula holds: $c[\theta_s\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]=v+vs=v(1+s)=c[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]\cdot(1+s)$ by [F2], using that right multiplication by $s$ in $\mathbb Z[W]$ sends the basis element $v$ to $vs$. Since $\theta_s$ is exact by [F2] it induces an additive endomorphism of $K_0$; agreement on the standard basis [F1] gives $c[\theta_sX]=c[X](1+s)$ for all $X\in\mathcal O_\lambda$, and both sides are additive in $X$.

Iterate step 2.1 along the word, applying the factors in the order in which they act: the composite $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$ applies $\theta_{s_1}$ first, so $c[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(((1+s_1))(1+s_2))\cdots(1+s_k)=(1+s_1)(1+s_2)\cdots(1+s_k)$; expanding the product gives the sum over all subwords $s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, $i_1<\cdots<i_r$, of their products, with the multiplicity with which each product arises. The full subword contributes $w$ once; every proper subword has strictly smaller length, and its product is $\le w$ with smaller length, hence strictly smaller than $w$ in the Bruhat order by [F3]. Reversing the order of composition multiplies the factors in the reverse order, as recorded.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of
the Cartan subalgebra of [[def-bgg-category-o]], graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$
as fixed on this page ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]],
[[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]). Let
$\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$
by
$$x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak h),\qquad x\cdot(s\otimes1)=0\quad(x\in\mathfrak n^+),$$
where for $x\in\mathfrak h$, $xs$ means multiplication by the
linear polynomial $x\in S(\mathfrak h)$; $\mathfrak n^+$ acts trivially. Put
$$M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda),$$
a module over $\mathfrak g\otimes S$: the left $\mathfrak g$-action is induced,
and $S$ acts on the right by multiplication on the last factor, which commutes
with $\mathfrak g$. Specializing at a closed point $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$ gives
$$M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon),$$
the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]; this is the universal family of
Verma modules with deformation parameter $\epsilon$.

**The family.** For a localization $T$ of $S$ put
$M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$, and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the
full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of
a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak g$-modules $E$. Write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for
$R=S_{(0)}$, the localization of $S$ at the origin of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment
$T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} T$. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents of highest weights
$\lambda+\nu+\epsilon$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors, and they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and the distinct constituent labels have distinct central characters at the
generic parameter: an equality $\lambda+\gamma+\tau+\rho=w(\lambda+\gamma'+\tau+\rho)$
as affine functions of $\tau$ forces $w=1$ by comparing linear parts,
and then $\gamma=\gamma'$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]).

**Selected components.** For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] and a
dot-dominant integral target $\nu$, so that $\nu+\rho$ lies in the closed
positive chamber, denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ the component of
$\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber at the origin lies in the selected
target block $\mathcal O_\nu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Finite Verma flags of the
deformed tensor products and pairwise-unit resultants of their
central-character polynomials define this component by actual central
idempotents over $R$, obtained from [[thm-chinese-remainder-theorem-for-comaximal-ideals]].
Indeed choose a linear combination $z$ of central elements separating the
finitely many distinct special characters. On each deformed Verma factor,
$z$ acts by a polynomial $c_i(\tau)$ by
[[lem-harish-chandra-projection-computes-highest-weight-scalars]], and a flag
is annihilated by $\prod_i(z-c_i(\tau))$. Group these factors by their
constant values at the origin; differences from different groups are units
in $R$, so their product polynomials are comaximal in $R[X]$. CRT gives
mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors, whose images are the selected
components and whose sum is the identity. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor
family; thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are
distinguished.

**Weight structure.** Write $\tau:\mathfrak h\to T$ for the tautological linear map.
Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry a **deformed weight decomposition**
$X=\bigoplus_\xi X^\xi$, where
$$X^\xi=\{m:(h-\tau(h))m=\xi(h)m\text{ for every }h\in\mathfrak h\}.$$
These are eigenmodules for $h-\tau(h)$, not ordinary complex weight spaces
for $h$. They are finite projective, hence locally free of finite rank over $T$, as follows from the PBW model of Verma modules and the
flatness of the localization
([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, $S=S(\mathfrak g)$ the symmetric algebra of the adjoint
representation, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$ its invariants, $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ the
center of the enveloping algebra, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ be a Kostant
harmonic subspace, so that multiplication is an isomorphism
$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\to S$ of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules with $R$
acting trivially ([[thm-kostant-harmonic-decomposition-of-the-symmetric-algebra]]).

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ with zero-weight space
$E_0$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)$ is a free graded
$R$-module of rank $\dim E_0$, and the module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is a free $Z$-module of
rank $\dim E_0$; with the filtered lifting $U(\mathfrak g)=Z\cdot\operatorname{sym}(\mathcal H)$
of [[thm-enveloping-algebra-is-free-over-its-center]] these freenesses are
compatible with the natural quotient maps. More precisely,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\cong R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))\cong Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),$$
where $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H)$ is a finite-dimensional
graded vector space of dimension $\dim E_0$; consequently every central
reduction has adjoint $E$-multiplicity $\dim E_0$, and the natural map
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\otimes_R R/R_+\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S/(R_+S))$
is an isomorphism onto a space of dimension $\dim E_0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g)$ is a free left, hence also right, module over its center $Z(U(\mathfrak g))$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, set $S=S(\mathfrak g)$, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$, and let $\mathcal H$ be its Kostant harmonic subspace. Multiplication is an isomorphism
$$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S$$
of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules, where $R$ carries the trivial action. The assertion includes $\mathfrak g=0$.

Orbit sums indexed by the distinct $W$-orbits in $P$ form a complex vector-space basis of $\mathbb C[P]^W$. Equivalently they are indexed by dominant integral weights, with exactly one per orbit, including weights on chamber walls. Every invariant has finite support in this basis.

For each dominant $\lambda$, the set of dominant $\mu\le\lambda$ is finite. In fact every such $\mu$ satisfies $\|\mu\|\le\|\lambda\|$ for the specified invariant Euclidean norm. All assertions are choice-free.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Work first over the polynomial ring $S$, before localizing. Put $G=F\otimes E^*$. Tensor-Hom adjunction identifies the stated tensor-object Hom module with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes S}(M_S(\lambda),G\otimes M_S(\lambda))$. A map is determined by a singular vector in the finite free deformed weight space of relative weight $\lambda$; the simple raising equations give a finite polynomial matrix $A$. The PBW model [F1] supplies the domain and codomain bases.

Every complex point of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ gives kernel dimension $\dim G_0$ by [F2], so $A$ has the same rank $s$ at every such point. Every $(s+1)$-minor therefore vanishes as a polynomial; the $s$-minors generate the unit ideal, because otherwise a maximal ideal containing them would be an evaluation ideal by [[cor-weak-nullstellensatz-algebraically-closed-coordinate-form]], contradicting rank $s$ there. On an open where an $s$-minor is invertible, row and column elimination gives $\operatorname{diag}(I_s,0)$. Thus the kernel is finite projective of rank $\dim G_0$ and commutes with arbitrary base change. This argument is over $S$, so it applies to every localization $T$, even one whose closed points are not complex evaluation points.

For each finite-dimensional simple $L$, the adjoint $L$-multiplicity module of $U\otimes_ZS$ is $S\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(L,\mathcal H)$ by the harmonic decomposition [F3] and [F2]; it is finite free of rank $\dim L_0$. The action maps it to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(L,\operatorname{End}_S M_S(\lambda))$, which by tensor-Hom adjunction is the kernel from step 2.1 for $G=L^*$. At every complex point this map is an isomorphism by Duflo–Joseph [F2]. Its cokernel is finite and vanishes by local Nakayama at every maximal ideal of $S$; the resulting surjection splits onto the projective target, and its kernel, a projective module of rank zero, vanishes on each local free chart. Hence it is an isomorphism. Localizing gives the same result over $T$. Finite-dimensional complete reducibility decomposes every finite adjoint submodule, so these isotypic isomorphisms prove (1).

For $G=F\otimes E^*$, tensor-Hom adjunction identifies the tensor-object Hom module with the adjoint $G^*$-multiplicity module of the endomorphism algebra in (1). Step 3.1 makes it free of rank $\dim G_0=\dim(E\otimes F^*)_0$; equality of the last dimensions follows by dualizing $G$. Step 2.1 proves its base-change assertion. Finite sums distribute over Hom, and for summands a Hom module is the image of the split idempotent $f\mapsto e_Nfe_M$ on an ambient Hom module. Such images are finite projective and commute with every base change. This proves (2) and (3) without claiming that arbitrary projective modules over arbitrary localizations are free.

Over the local ring $R$ at the origin, the deformed weight spaces of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ are finite projective, hence finite free: lift a residue basis, use Nakayama for a surjection from a free module, split it by projectivity, and apply Nakayama to the complementary kernel. A map whose residue fiber is an isomorphism has invertible determinant on each such weight space, so it has a weightwise inverse. The inverses commute with the $\mathfrak g$-action because the original map does. This proves (4). AC is inherited from the named suppliers.

The reader polynomial-first minors argument is locally sound: constant kernel rank at every complex polynomial point makes the higher minors zero and the rank minors a unit ideal before localization, hence kernel commutes with arbitrary residues. Harmonic isotypic action maps would make tensor-object Hom free; split idempotents give finite projective summand Hom and weightwise local Nakayama detects an existing inverse. Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over
$\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left
$C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence
$$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$
The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions
of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated
$C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the
regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new
top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying
$V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the
inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply
self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$,
with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the
projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with
Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral
block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$ the localization at the origin, and use the selected
component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed
family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]. For
every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed
$\lambda$-block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to
isomorphism, and every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one
of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same
multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this
block is a direct summand of a finite sum of truncated induced projectives
representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras
$R\to R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_RR'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_RR',N\otimes_RR').$$
For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$ this Hom module is finite free over
local $R$. A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such finite
projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is
itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target
$\nu$, including singular $\nu$, the same local projective construction gives
all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$;
these lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ of a
regular-source tensor family. It is neither necessary nor asserted that the
singular Verma itself generates every target projective, and the other central
components of the full tensor family are not claimed to have only these
indecomposables.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed
antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S^W$
for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
$\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+\rho+\epsilon)$, and define
$$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))\otimes r.$$
Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$
are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra
isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$
On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$
acts by the scalar
$\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(x(\lambda+\rho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$;
these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on
$P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the
endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant
integral $\nu$ the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where
$W_\nu$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the
singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted
Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion
$R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection
$s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural
isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules
$$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$
Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule
$C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the
second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the
left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; read up to the auxiliary suspension
normalisation fixed by the rank-one case, the right origin reduction of $B_s$
is the two-dimensional module of centered degrees $-1,1$, for $M=S$ the
coinvariant reduction satisfies
$B_s\otimes_SC\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)$ in the same normalisation, and
$B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the
former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension
$2|W|$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$
formula, and no grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted.

**Graphs and supports.** Keep $k=\mathbb Q$, $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with
$\deg x_i=2$, and the affine scheme $V=\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}R$,
whose $k$-points are $V(k)=k^n$. Use the place-permuting action of $S_n$
from [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]].
For $w\in S_n$ let
$$Gr(w):=\operatorname{Graph}(w:V\to V)\subseteq V\times_kV,\quad Gr(w)(k)=\{(w\lambda,\lambda):\lambda\in k^n\},\qquad Gr(A):=\bigcup_{w\in A}Gr(w)\ \ (A\subseteq S_n),$$
so that $V\times_kV=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kR)$ and $Gr(w)$ is the graph
of the map $\lambda\mapsto w\lambda$. A graded $(R,R)$-bimodule $M$ is the
same thing as a graded module over $R\otimes_kR$, and the support of $m\in M$ is
the zero set $\operatorname{supp}(m):=V(\operatorname{Ann}(m))\subseteq V\times V$
of its annihilator ideal in $R\otimes_kR$. For $A\subseteq S_n$ put
$$\Gamma_AM:=\{m\in M:\operatorname{supp}(m)\subseteq Gr(A)\},$$
a graded sub-bimodule of $M$. Since $Gr(A)$ is closed with radical ideal
$I(Gr(A))=\bigcap_{w\in A}I(Gr(w))$ (an intersection of prime ideals, since each
$Gr(w)$ is a linear subspace of $V\times V$ complementing the second factor), an
element $m$ lies in $\Gamma_AM$ exactly when $I(Gr(A))^N m=0$ for some $N\ge0$:
this is the Nullstellensatz together with the Noetherianity of
$R\otimes_kR$. The ideal itself need not annihilate such an element — in
$(R\otimes_kR)/I(Gr(e))^2$ the class of $1$ is supported on $Gr(e)$ but is not
killed by $I(Gr(e))$ — which is why the criterion is stated with a power of the
ideal. For $i\in\mathbb Z$ we write
$$\Gamma_{\ge i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\ge i\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\le i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\le i\}}M,$$
using the length function of [[lem-type-a-reduced-words-are-connected-by-braid-moves]],
while for $y\in S_n$ the $y$-indexed symbols denote the *Bruhat
principal-set* cutoffs of Soergel's Notation 6.1,
$$\Gamma_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\le y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{<y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x<y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\ge y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{>y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x>y\}}M,$$
with $\Gamma_yM:=\Gamma_{\{y\}}M$ the elements concentrated on the single graph
$Gr(y)$ and $\Gamma_{\ne y}M:=\Gamma_{S_n\setminus\{y\}}M$ the elements
concentrated off $Gr(y)$. The integer-indexed symbols of the previous display are
the *length* cutoffs used to define the flags below, and they must not be
confused with the element-indexed Bruhat cutoffs: for $y=s_1$ in $S_4$ the
submodule $\Gamma_{\le1}M$ contains $Gr(s_3)$ while
$\Gamma_{\le y}M=\Gamma_{\{e,s_1\}}M$ does not, and the two cutoffs agree at
the extremes, $\Gamma_{\le w_0}=\Gamma_{\le\ell(w_0)}=M$ and
$\Gamma_{<e}=\Gamma_{\le-1}=0$. So
$\Gamma^yM:=M/\Gamma_{\ne y}M$ is Soergel's $y$-layer
*quotient*; following Soergel's
Notation 6.1 we write the two $y$-layer quotients with an underline,
$$\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\le y}M/\Gamma_{<y}M,\qquad \underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\ge y}M/\Gamma_{>y}M,$$
so that $\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M$ is the quotient of the lower support
submodule by $\Gamma_{<y}M$ and $\underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M$ the quotient of
the upper support submodule by the part supported strictly above $Gr(y)$.

**Standard bimodules.** For $w\in S_n$ let $R_w$ be the graded $(R,R)$-bimodule
which equals $R$ as a graded $k$-vector space and has
$$f\cdot x=fx,\qquad x\cdot g=w(g)\,x\qquad(f,g,x\in R),$$
where $w(g)(\lambda):=g(w^{-1}\lambda)$; $R_w$ is generated by the element $1$ of
degree $0$. Write $(k)$ for the *external* shift $M(k):=M\{-k\}$ of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]], so that
$M(k)_d=M_{d+k}$; this is the shift convention of the type-A sources, and it is
the one in which $B_i=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1)$ of
[[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]] has $1\otimes1$ of
degree $-1$. Put
$$\Delta_w(d):=R_w(d-\ell(w)),\qquad \nabla_w(d):=R_w(d+\ell(w))\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$
so that $\Delta_w(d)$ is the standard bimodule $R_w$ with its generator in
degree $\ell(w)-d$, and $\nabla_w(d)$ is $R_w$ with its generator in degree
$-\ell(w)-d$. Thus $\Delta_w(0)=R_w\{\ell(w)\}$,
$\nabla_w(0)=R_w\{-\ell(w)\}$ and $\Delta_e(d)=\nabla_e(d)=R(d)$ is generated
in degree $-d$; in particular $\Delta_e(0)=\nabla_e(0)=R_e=R$.

For graded free $R$-modules in this type-A page, a homogeneous free generator of degree $a$ contributes $v^a$ to graded rank. This is the $v\mapsto v^{-1}$ transform of Soergel's rank convention in his Notation 5.2; all rank formulas below use this convention.

**Support filtrations.** A $\Delta$-flag of a graded $R$-bimodule $M$ is a
finite chain $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_k=M$ of graded
sub-bimodules which refines the length filtration
$$M=\Gamma_{\ge0}M\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge1}M\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge\ell(w_0)+1}M=0$$
of $M$ (here $\Gamma_{\ge0}M=M$ for every bimodule supported on
$Gr(S_n)=\bigcup_{w}Gr(w)$, which all bimodules of this page are, and
$\Gamma_{\ge i}M=0$ for $i>\ell(w_0)$ because no graph $Gr(x)$ with
$\ell(x)>i$ remains) and whose successive quotients are
standard bimodules $M_j/M_{j-1}\cong R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$. We require each
length layer to be a finite direct sum of shifted graph bimodules of that
length, as in Soergel's Definition 5.4. Thus the
quotients carry a numbering with $\ell(x_1)\ge\cdots\ge\ell(x_k)$ and each
$R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$ is one graph, so that $M$ has a "support flag" in the sense of
Soergel's $F_\Delta$. A $\nabla$-flag has the same direct-sum condition on its length layers, with the reverse length
filtration $\Gamma_{\le i}M$ and $\ell(x_1)\le\cdots\le\ell(x_k)$. The
refinement condition is a condition on supports, not an ordering of incomparable
quotients of equal length; only the lengths are ordered. For $i=\ell(x)$ the
graded multiplicity is
$$(M:\Delta_x(d)):=\text{multiplicity of }\Delta_x(d)\text{ in } \Gamma_{\ge i}M/\Gamma_{\ge i+1}M,$$
and, for a $\nabla$-flag, $(M:\nabla_x(d))$ is the multiplicity of
$\nabla_x(d)$ in $\Gamma_{\le i}M/\Gamma_{\le i-1}M$; a priori both symbols
refer to a chosen compatible enumeration (the next items on this page prove that
they do not depend on it). With $T_x$ the Hecke basis of
[[lem-type-a-hecke-standard-basis-for-soergel-comparison]] and
$\widetilde T_x:=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$, the character sums attached to a flag are
$$h_\Delta(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\Delta_x(d))\,v^d\,\widetilde T_x,\qquad h_\nabla(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\nabla_x(d))\,v^{-d}\,\widetilde T_x,$$
and they are used only through the items that prove these sums intrinsic.

**Small $n$.** For $n\le1$ there is a single element $e$ and every object is a finite direct sum of shifts $\bigoplus_j R(d_j)$. Its one-graph flags have these summands as quotients, so $h_\Delta=\sum_jv^{d_j}\widetilde T_e$ and $h_\nabla=\sum_jv^{-d_j}\widetilde T_e$; in particular both characters send the unit $R$ to $1$.

**The reduction.** Work over the ring $S=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ of the real
scalar-extension definition ([[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]]),
with $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ the ideal of positive-degree elements; the residue
field of the right action is
$$k:=S/S_+=\mathbb R,$$
with quotient map $S\twoheadrightarrow k$, $s\mapsto \bar s$. For a graded
$(S,S)$-bimodule $M$ that is finite free as a right $S$-module put
$$\overline M:=M\otimes_Sk=M/MS_+,$$
the **reduction** of $M$: a finite-dimensional graded $k$-vector space, on which
the left $S$-action descends because $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $MS_+$ is
stable under left multiplication. Write $\overline M^{\,i}$ for its homogeneous
component of degree $i$, $d_i(M):=\dim_{\mathbb R}\overline M^{\,i}$ for the
graded dimensions, and
$$\dim\overline M:=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}d_i(M)\,v^{-i}$$
for the **graded dimension** (a finite Laurent polynomial); all tensor products
below are over $S$. For a morphism $f:M\to M'$ of graded bimodules, i.e. a
degree-zero bi-$S$-linear map, the induced map
$$\overline f:\overline M\to\overline{M'},\qquad \overline f(m+MS_+):=f(m)+M'S_+ ,$$
is well defined and $k$-linear of degree zero, because $f(MS_+)\subseteq M'S_+$.
Reduction is a functor from finite right-free graded bimodules to finite
dimensional graded $k$-vector spaces; it preserves finite direct sums and
shifts, in the sense $\overline{M(d)}=\overline M(d)$ in the Elias-Williamson
shift convention $M(d)_e=M_{d+e}$.

**The dominant Lefschetz operator.** Fix a strictly dominant degree-two
element
$$\rho=\sum_{j=1}^nc_jx_j\in S_2,\qquad c_1>c_2>\cdots>c_n ,$$
which exists by [[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]] (for
example $c_j=(n+1)/2-j$); recall that this is exactly the condition
$\rho(\alpha_i^\vee)>0$ for every simple coroot $\alpha_i^\vee$ in the
coordinate normalization of this page
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]). Let
$\rho\cdot(-):M\to M$, $m\mapsto\rho m$, denote left multiplication by $\rho$.
Since $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $\rho\,(MS_+)\subseteq MS_+$, this
operator preserves the submodule $MS_+$ and therefore descends to a degree-two
$k$-linear endomorphism
$$L_0:=\rho\cdot(-):\overline M\longrightarrow\overline M,\qquad m+MS_+\longmapsto \rho m+MS_+,$$
called the **dominant Lefschetz operator** on $\overline M$. For rational
objects $B_x,B_s$ with real scalar extensions
$B_x^R=B_x\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$ and $B_s^R$, the same construction
applies to the reduced tensor product
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}=\overline{(B_xB_s)^R}$, where $B_xB_s$ denotes the
tensor product over the rational polynomial ring; the operator $L_0$ on it is
the value $\zeta=0$ of the deformed operator $L_\zeta$ defined later on this
page.

**Descent detection.** For every $w\in S_n$ and every simple reflection $s_i$
one has
$$(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ell(s_iw)>\ell(w).$$
Indeed, $(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}$ is positive
exactly when $w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1)$, the left-ascent criterion for inversion
length. Thus the displayed evaluation detects left descents; applied to
$w=x^{-1}$ it detects right descents of $x$, because $\ell(s_ix^{-1})=\ell(xs_i)$.

**Grading conventions.** The reduced module $\overline{B_x^R}$ has bottom degree
$-\ell(x)$ and top degree $+\ell(x)$; the unreduced bimodule has nonzero
components in arbitrarily high degrees. On a reduced module the "centered" degree $-i$ is the
internal degree $-i$, and the Lefschetz operator raises internal degree by two.
All homological (complex) shifts are written $[\,j\,]$ and all internal shifts
$(d)$, as on the rest of this page; the Bruhat order used throughout is the
rank-inequality order of
[[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]].

Let $B_w$ be the rational indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule and let $B_w^R$ be its real scalar extension. (1) $B_w^R$ is indecomposable; its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local with residue field $\mathbb R$. If $S(w)$ holds, its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is $\mathbb R$, but no rank-one assertion for the full graded endomorphism module is made. (2) Real extension preserves the labels and shifts of all finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions of rational Soergel bimodules, and every real indecomposable is a unique $B_w^R(d)$. (3) $\Delta$/$\nabla$ support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reduction by positive-degree right polynomials, and Hom spaces commute with scalar extension; thus character identities over $\mathbb R$ descend to $\mathbb Q$. (4) If $xs>x$ and $S(y)$ holds for all $y<xs$, then $B_xB_s=B_{xs}\oplus\bigoplus_{y<xs}B_y^{a_y}$ with $a_y$ nonnegative integers and no grading shifts; the top summand occurs once. If $xs<x$ and $S(x)$ holds, then $B_xB_s=B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$. All assertions concern the normalized self-dual indecomposables.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex
semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block
and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$.
Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan
reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then:

(1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention,
followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
(multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel;

(2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$
identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective,
canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its
isomorphism class;

(3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the
coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or
used.

This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral
case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the
invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block
with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor
$V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant
algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]],
so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$
and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map
$$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of
objects killed by $V$.

derivations.claim: The functor $V_R$ is exact and sends each deformed standard $\Delta_R(y\cdot\lambda)$ to a finite free $R$-module of rank one: by [F4] its closed fiber is one-dimensional, and by [F2] the Hom module into the Verma-filtered standard is finite free with base change, so the rank is one.

On that rank-one free module the center acts on the generic constituent of highest weight $y\cdot\lambda+\tau$ by the scalar $\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(y(\lambda+\rho)+\tau)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(y^{-1}\tau)$, which in the polynomial graph convention [F3] is the branch of the graph label $x=y^{-1}$; hence the graph label of the standard constituent is the inverse of its highest-weight label.

The preceding dictionary proves the deformed, action-compatible wall isomorphism $V_R\theta_s\cong R\otimes_{R^s}V_R$ by adjunction, the translated central inclusion and the coefficient-of-$\alpha_s$ Frobenius pairing; it also proves deformed full faithfulness and the natural reduction-of-Hom map. Iteration identifies the localized polynomial word with the $V_R$-image of its lifted projective word. The unique top-label polynomial summand and the top projective summand match under this full faithfulness, by the dictionary's length induction. Multiplication gives a vector-space isomorphism

$$U(\mathfrak n^-)\xrightarrow{\sim}M(\lambda),\qquad u\longmapsto uv_\lambda.$$

Consequently, ordered negative-root PBW monomials from
[[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] applied to
$v_\lambda$ form a basis.

Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be an ordered basis of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$. Then the monomials

$$x_1^{a_1}x_2^{a_2}\cdots x_r^{a_r} \qquad (a_i\in \mathbb N_0)$$

form a basis of $U(\mathfrak g)$. In particular, multiplication identifies $\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak g)$ with the symmetric algebra $S(\mathfrak g)$ on the symbols of the $x_i$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Every object of $\mathcal O$ has a finite composition series and is both Noetherian and Artinian. The length of zero is zero.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The simple objects of $\mathcal O$ are exactly the modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, and $L(\lambda)\cong L(\mu)$ if and only if $\lambda=\mu$. Simplicity here excludes zero.
Every nonzero $\mathfrak g$-homomorphism $M(\mu)\to M(\lambda)$ is injective.

For a $\mathfrak g$-module $V$, sending a homomorphism $T:M(\lambda)\to V$
to $T(v_\lambda)$ is a bijection onto the vectors $v\in V$ of weight
$\lambda$ annihilated by $\mathfrak n^+$.  Here $M(\lambda)$ is
[[def-verma-module]].  The nonzero vectors in this target are precisely the
highest-weight vectors of weight $\lambda$ from
[[def-highest-weight-vector-and-cyclic-highest-weight-module]]; the zero vector
corresponds to the zero homomorphism.
For all weights $\lambda,\mu$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),M(\lambda))\leq1$.

There is a unique Chevalley-contravariant bilinear form $S_\lambda$ on
$M(\lambda)$ with $S_\lambda(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$.

The radical of $S_\lambda$ is $J(\lambda)$, the unique maximal submodule.
Thus $S_\lambda$ descends to a nondegenerate form on $L(\lambda)$.

Restricted Chevalley duality is an exact contravariant equivalence $D:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}}$, with a natural isomorphism $D^2\cong\operatorname{id}$. It preserves each weight-space dimension, the formal character, and every simple composition multiplicity.

The assignments on $x\in\mathfrak g$

$$\Delta(x)=\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)\otimes1+1\otimes\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x),\qquad \varepsilon(x)=0,\qquad S(x)=-\iota_{\mathfrak g}(x)$$

extend to the standard cocommutative Hopf-algebra structure on
$U(\mathfrak g)$. The first two assignments are Lie maps into the commutator
algebras of $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes U(\mathfrak g)$ and $k$, so enveloping
universality extends them to algebra maps. Interpreting the last assignment as
a Lie map into $U(\mathfrak g)^{\mathrm{op}}$ extends it to an algebra map into
the opposite algebra, equivalently an anti-algebra map $S$.

Coassociativity, cocommutativity, and the counit identities follow because the
corresponding algebra maps agree on every generator. For the antipode, write
$\Delta(a)=\sum a_{(1)}\otimes a_{(2)}$. Both convolution identities hold on
$1$ and on every generator, since multiplying
$-x\otimes1+1\otimes x$ gives zero. If they hold for $a$ and $b$, then

$$\sum S(a_{(1)}b_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\sum S(b_{(1)})S(a_{(1)})a_{(2)}b_{(2)}=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1,$$

and similarly

$$\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(a_{(2)}b_{(2)})=\sum a_{(1)}b_{(1)}S(b_{(2)})S(a_{(2)})=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)1.$$

Induction on word length and linearity therefore prove both antipode
identities on all of $U(\mathfrak g)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, $S=S(\mathfrak g)$ the symmetric algebra of the adjoint
representation, $R=S^{\mathfrak g}$ its invariants, $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ the
center of the enveloping algebra, and let $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ be a Kostant
harmonic subspace, so that multiplication is an isomorphism
$R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\to S$ of graded $\mathfrak g$-modules with $R$
acting trivially ([[thm-kostant-harmonic-decomposition-of-the-symmetric-algebra]]).

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ with zero-weight space
$E_0$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)$ is a free graded
$R$-module of rank $\dim E_0$, and the module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is a free $Z$-module of
rank $\dim E_0$; with the filtered lifting $U(\mathfrak g)=Z\cdot\operatorname{sym}(\mathcal H)$
of [[thm-enveloping-algebra-is-free-over-its-center]] these freenesses are
compatible with the natural quotient maps. More precisely,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\cong R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))\cong Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H),$$
where $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\mathcal H)$ is a finite-dimensional
graded vector space of dimension $\dim E_0$; consequently every central
reduction has adjoint $E$-multiplicity $\dim E_0$, and the natural map
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S)\otimes_R R/R_+\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,S/(R_+S))$
is an isomorphism onto a space of dimension $\dim E_0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$,
and let $p_1,\dots,p_r$ be homogeneous basic generators of $S(\mathfrak g)^{\mathfrak g}$
of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$, corresponding by Chevalley restriction to basic Weyl
invariants ([[thm-symmetric-invariants-restrict-to-weyl-invariants]],
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]). Put
$$A=S(\mathfrak g)/(p_1,\dots,p_r).$$ Then $A$ is a reduced integral domain of
dimension $\dim\mathfrak g-r=2|\Phi^+|$, with Hilbert series
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(A,t)=\frac{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{d_i})}{(1-t)^{\dim\mathfrak g}},$$
and for every central character $\chi:Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\mathbb C$ the PBW
associated graded of $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ is canonically
isomorphic to $A$.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module of highest weight $\lambda$. Then the quadratic Casimir element acts on $M$ by the scalar

$$ (\lambda,\lambda+2\rho), $$

where the pairing on $\mathfrak h^*$ is induced by the Killing form and $\rho$ is the Weyl vector from [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]].
For all weights $\lambda,\mu$, $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),M(\lambda))\leq1$.

derivations.claim: If $\mathfrak g=0$ then $U(\mathfrak g)=\mathbb C$, $M(\mu)=\mathbb C$ and everything is immediate; assume $\mathfrak g\neq0$, so $N=\dim\mathfrak n^->0$. By [F2] the Verma module $M(\mu)$ has finite length, so it contains a simple submodule; by [F2] every simple object is some $L(\eta)$ and the universal map $M(\eta)\to L(\eta)\hookrightarrow M(\mu)$ is injective; hence $M(\mu)$ contains $M(\eta)$ for a highest weight $\eta$. Writing $M(\mu)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ by [F1], the submodule generated by the singular vector $p\,v_\mu$ is $U(\mathfrak n^-)p$: its embedding is right multiplication $u\mapsto up$ by a nonzero element $p\in U(\mathfrak n^-)$.

Growth: the PBW filtration of $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ has $\dim F_nU(\mathfrak n^-)$ asymptotic to $n^N/N!$, while the quotient $U(\mathfrak n^-)/U(\mathfrak n^-)p$ has associated graded $S(\mathfrak n^-)/(\bar p)$ for the nonzero leading form $\bar p$ of $p$, so its Hilbert series is of the form $(1-t^d)/(1-t)^N$ and $\dim(U(\mathfrak n^-)/U(\mathfrak n^-)p)_{\le n}=O(n^{N-1})$; the same bound therefore holds for $M(\mu)/M(\eta)$ and, after tensoring by the finite-dimensional $E$, for $E\otimes(M(\mu)/M(\eta))$, because $\dim(E\otimes X)_{\le n}\le(\dim E)\dim X_{\le n}$.

The diagonal $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-action makes $E\otimes M(\mu)$ a free $U(\mathfrak n^-)$-module of rank $\dim E$, by [F5] applied to the identification $M(\mu)\cong U(\mathfrak n^-)$ of [F1]. In particular every nonzero vector $x$ of $E\otimes M(\mu)$ generates a copy $U(\mathfrak n^-)x$ of the domain $U(\mathfrak n^-)$, of growth $n^N$.

The Hom space as a kernel: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))$ is the space of $\mathfrak n^+$-invariants in the weight-$\mu$ space $(E\otimes M(\mu))_\mu$, i.e. the kernel of the finitely many raising maps $e_i:(E\otimes M(\mu))_\mu	o(E\otimes M(\mu))_{\mu+\alpha_i}$. This weight space has $\mu$-independent dimension $\sum_

Simple-Verma case: if $M(\mu)=L(\mu)$ is simple, then $D\,M(\mu)=M(\mu)$ by [F4] and $M(\mu)=
abla(\mu)$, and the tensor-hom adjunction plus [F4] give $$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E^{*}\otimes M(\mu),M(\mu)),$$ which is the multiplicity of $\Delta(\mu)$ in the standard flag of $E^{*}\otimes M(\mu)$, namely $\dim E^{*}_0=\dim E_0$: by [F4] the flag factors are the $\Delta(\mu+

Lower bound for all $\mu$: first the weights of simple Verma modules are Zariski dense. Indeed, if a Verma module has a nonzero proper submodule, choose a nonzero weight vector of minimal positive height $\beta\in Q^+\setminus\{0\}$ in it; every simple-root raising operator kills this vector, whose weight is $\mu-\beta$. The Casimir scalar on its cyclic highest-weight submodule equals that on $M(\mu)$, so [F7] gives $2(\mu+\rho,\beta)=(\beta,\beta)$. On the real root span the pairing is positive definite; this equality is impossible when $(\mu+\rho,\alpha_i)<0$ for every simple root. This nonempty real open chamber therefore consists of simple-Verma weights and is Zariski dense, since a complex polynomial vanishing on a real open set vanishes identically. The polynomial matrix of step 1.4 has a nonempty Zariski-open maximal-rank locus, which meets this dense set. At such an intersection step 1.5 gives kernel dimension $\dim E_0$; rank can only decrease at other weights, so $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))\ge\dim E_0$ for every $\mu$.

Upper bound: the restriction map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\eta),E\otimes M(\eta))$$ is injective. Second, if $\varphi\neq0$ killed $M(\eta)$, it would factor through $M(\mu)/M(\eta)$ and its nonzero image would contain, by step 1.3, a copy of the domain $U(\mathfrak n^-)$ of growth $n^N$, again contradicting step 1.2.

Combining steps 1.5, 2.1 and 2.2, $$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$$ for every highest weight $\mu$ and every finite-dimensional $E$; the same computation with $E$ replaced by its dual identifies the adjoint isotypic multiplicity in $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules with $\dim E_0$, by the freeness statement of [F6].

Suppose the action had nonzero kernel $K$ in $U_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Then the associated graded $\operatorname{gr}(K)$ is a nonzero graded ideal of the domain $A$ of [F6], so it contains $Af$ for a nonzero homogeneous $f$; multiplication by $f$ is injective and the complete-intersection Hilbert series of $A$ gives $\dim(A/Af)_{\le n}=O(n^{2N-1})$.
